introduction_markdown:
**General Certificate of Education Board - Advanced Level Examination. Information and Communication Technologies (0796), Paper 3 (practical), June 2022. Duration: two hours. Answer ALL tasks.**

The booklet reproduced here contains two versions of the same practical paper, headed Group 1 and Group 2: they have the same two tasks (Task A: spreadsheet; Task B: programming) with a few differences in wording, and a different algorithm in Task B.

Enter the information required in the shaded boxes. Do not write in pencil. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answer. Your results must be recorded in the spaces provided in this question booklet. Candidates must allow for themselves enough time to complete and check their work where these are required. The supervisor will guide you on how to save your files but usually you will be expected to save all your work in one folder named *Candidate folder* that will be created in your desktop. When an imperative programming language is required to write program code, either Standard [ISO] Pascal or [ANSI] C programming language may be used. You should ensure all your work is collected and printed before leaving the examination room. All printed work should be inserted in this booklet and well stapled. Carefully handle all equipment put at your disposal to avoid accidents that may lead to a disaster or system failure. Report any case of system or device malfunction to your supervisor.

The working file (the SALES workbook) is supplied on the day in the Candidate folder; it is not reproduced in the printed paper.

questions.enonce_markdown:
The algorithm given by a student to solve a certain problem.

```
Start
    Output: Give the unit price, of the item
    Input: Get the unit price, U, from the keyboard
    Output: Give the quantity of item bought
    Input: Get the quantity, Q, from the keyboard
    Set the total, T, to U*Q
    Print T.
Stop.
```

Explain the objective of the algorithm. *[2 marks]*

*(answer lines: write the answer in the lines provided)*
questions.corrige_markdown:
The objective of the algorithm is to **calculate and display the total price of an item bought**. It asks the user for the unit price (U) and for the quantity bought (Q), multiplies them (T = U x Q) and prints the result T. For example, 7 items at a unit price of 11 give a total of 77.

*Marking:* 1 mark for the idea of calculating the total (price) of the purchase, 1 mark for the data used (unit price and quantity, entered from the keyboard) or the operation (product U x Q).

questions.enonce_markdown:
Identify the variables and give their respective data types of the program that will implement the above algorithm. *[2 marks]*

Variable 1 ........ Data type ........

Variable 2 ........ Data type ........

*(answer lines: write the answer in the lines provided)*
questions.corrige_markdown:
The algorithm manipulates three variables, each of which becomes a declared variable of the program:

| Variable | Meaning | Data type |
|---|---|---|
| `U` | unit price of the item | real (`float` in C, `real` in Pascal) |
| `Q` | quantity of item bought | integer (`int` in C, `integer` in Pascal) |
| `T` | total, T = U x Q | real (same type as the product U x Q) |

The quantity is a whole number of items, so it is an integer. The unit price may have decimals, so a real number is the safe type; with the test data of question 5 (whole numbers) an integer for U and T would also be accepted. The paper prints only two answer lines (Variable 1 and Variable 2), so any two of the three variables with a suitable type earn the marks; the total T is the third.

*Marking:* 1 mark for each variable with a suitable data type (2 marks in all).

questions.enonce_markdown:
Which control structure has been used in this algorithm? *[2 marks]*

*(answer line: write the answer in the line provided)*
questions.corrige_markdown:
The **sequence** (sequential) structure: the statements are executed one after the other, in the order in which they are written, from Start to Stop. The algorithm has no condition (no *selection*, such as IF ... THEN ... ELSE) and no loop (no *iteration*, such as WHILE or FOR): each instruction is carried out exactly once.

*Marking:* 1 mark for the name (sequence / sequential), 1 mark for the justification (instructions executed one after another, no choice and no repetition).

questions.enonce_markdown:
Implement the algorithm above using either C or Pascal programming language.

*You will be evaluated based on the following aspects: declaration of variables, presentation of I/O instructions, process instructions, understanding of syntax.*

Save your code using the file name *Calculator*. *[10 marks]*

Compile and execute using the following test data: U=11, Q=7; and write down the final result in the line below. *[3 marks]*

*(answer line: write the result in the line provided)*

**Print the source code of your program.**
questions.corrige_markdown:
Compile the program (for example `gcc Calculator.c -o Calculator` for C, `fpc Calculator.pas` for Pascal), run it and type the two test values when asked. The program multiplies 11 by 7:

```
Give the unit price of the item: 11
Give the quantity of item bought: 7
Total price = 77.00
```

The final result is **77** (displayed 77.00 with two decimal places; 77 if integer variables are used). Check: 11 x 7 = 77. The source code of the program is then printed (and, with the result, inserted in the booklet).

*Marking:* 1 mark for compiling without error, 1 mark for entering the test data U=11 and Q=7, 1 mark for the result 77.
